title: Conformal Limits of Critical Square-Lattice Random-Cluster Interfaces
main_claim: For every fixed q in [1,4], critical square-lattice FK Dobrushin interfaces converge to chordal SLE_kappa(q), with kappa(q)=4pi/arccos(-sqrt(q)/2), under uniform marked-Jordan approximation. The full nested free-plane loop collection converges to nested whole-plane CLE_kappa(q), keeping multiplicities and traversals. A corollary is Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges.

issues.location: observable.tex, Sec. 'Holomorphicity from reflection and extraction' (Prop. hol:mixed-bound, Lemma hol:templates); angular.tex final subsection 'Diagonal cuts and the physical reflection norm'
issues.description: This is not a demonstrated error; it marks where the audit could not go. The whole q<4 argument rests on one transfer: the infinite-plane operator-norm angular estimate (Thm bulk:angular-estimate) is moved to physical paired-wall diagrams with solid fragments, gaps and odd-reflection (conjugated) copies. That transfer is argued in prose: the 'tau stays +' claim after odd reflections, the common-scalar-phase claim from ice conservation, and the expected 1/2 even/odd copy count per feature. I could not check these line by line. The n^{-1-rho} times n^{-1+rho} times n^{-c0} count is internally consistent with what the summation by parts needs, which is o(n^{-2}) per stencil.
issues.evidence: 'After an odd number of reflections the local insertion is the L_+,Q^{-1} alternative; its angular parameter is still tau=+, with the reflected high coefficient.' ... 'Ice conservation therefore gives one common scalar phase, rather than term-dependent phases.'

coverage: I read the Introduction in full. In observable.tex I read Sec. 4 (tree lemma, marked values, compactness, diagonal residual, conditional boundary identification) and Sec. 7 (reflection/extraction, strict budget, templates, mixed-derivative bound, Theorem hol:disk). I read angular.tex Sec. 3.1-3.6 (R-matrix, plane Gram space, angle generator, edge-band continuation, inner factorization, Laurent/sandwich proof of the angular estimate), all of the logarithmic exponent comparisons in preliminaries.tex (rectangle, cylinder and charged-cylinder budgets, polygon corollary), and all of rotation-repair.tex (q=4 symmetry input for the six-vertex GFF theorem). Computational checks (python/mpmath): the four-change crossing formula at rho=1/3 equals Cardy's formula; at rho=1/4 it equals the Chelkak-Smirnov FK-Ising alternating-boundary crossing formula, and the f/(f+d(1-f)) wire renormalization gives a separate consistent value. Checked by hand: every entry of table four:table from w_e,k_e and Delta=pi/(2lambda)-3/2; the far-algebra identities; x^{2Delta}=-y^3; the Gamma identities and line-invariant constants on B and C; the polygon/strict budget arithmetic (3P+D*-P <= P); the Laurent exponent ordering (rho, 1-rho, 1+rho); the Schwarz-Christoffel angle sum; and the q=4 variance constant (unit-jump CLE4 heights give covariance -(1/pi^2)log, matching sqrt(2/pi) times the GFF with G=-(1/2pi)log). Not checked in detail: paired-wall tensor normalization and gap closure (observable Secs. 5-6), the current/path calculus (angular Sec. 4), the moving-domain and chordal driver transfer (chordal.tex), peeling/branching-SLE/CLE identification (peeling.tex), and the q=4 endpoint-field and rough-domain sections. The cited 2026 companion results (DCKKMO rotation coupling internals, SixVertexGFF2026 Thm 4.1/2.8) were taken as stated.
